subject: EdgeCloud renewal — proposed reserved augmentation & amendment terms
messages:
From: Samuel Price <samuel.price@edgecloud.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Rao <maya.rao@edgecloud.ai>, contracts@edgecloud.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal timeline — midterm capacity add?

Jonas —

Quick context: our Q2 usage is trending higher than forecasted and we need to add capacity ahead of the June renewal. We currently have a 48-GPU reserved pool (mixed A100/RTX) and want to top up by ~12 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs starting Apr 15.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood support a mid-term augmentation (add GPUs to the existing reserved pool) and pro-rate pricing for the remainder of the term?
- If we commit to the added capacity for the remaining 10 months, what discount can you offer vs standard on-demand top-up rates? We are also considering a 12-month step-up (extend the commit) if economics are favourable.

Also need throughput guarantees — currently we target 35k tokens/sec aggregate for model serving and need commitments on sustained throughput during peak windows.

Appreciate an outline + revised quote we can take to procurement.

— Samuel
Director, Platform Engineering
EdgeCloud

P.S. attaching a short usage export and the current SLO exceptions log for visibility (attached).

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Price <samuel.price@edgecloud.ai>
Cc: Maya Rao <maya.rao@edgecloud.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timeline — midterm capacity add?

Sam —

Thanks for the heads up and the usage export — helpful. Short answers up front: yes, we can do a mid-term augmentation and prorate the added reserved capacity for the remainder of your term. We can also structure a step-up to an extended 12-month commit if you prefer predictable pricing.

I'll outline two options in this thread:
1) Short-term augmentation (Apr 15 start): +12 GPUs reserved for remaining 10 months, prorated invoice. Pricing: top-up reserved rate = on-demand rate * 0.75 (i.e., 25% off on-demand) for the added pool. Includes standard Redwood throughput SLO (see notes). No change to existing commit.

2) Step-up commit: convert the +12 GPUs into a separate 12-month reserved commit (starts Apr 15). Pricing: committed rate = on-demand * 0.62 (38% off on-demand) if contract signed within 14 days. Includes a 99.9% regional throughput SLO with service credits for missed windows.

Throughput guarantees: we can commit to regional aggregate throughput targets (tokens/sec) and provide burst headroom via autoscaling/burst credits. For your 35k tokens/sec target we recommend the step-up commit (option 2) — it gives predictable unit economics and explicit SLA credits.

I'll loop in Karthik for pricing trenches and Marcus for legal/amendment steps. Expect a revised spreadsheet and a draft amendment by EOD tomorrow.

— Jonas
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_QoS_SLA_Summary.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 13:07:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: EdgeCloud augmentation — pricing options (internal)

Team —

Reviewed Sam's usage and Jonas' two-option approach. Quick internal notes:
- On-demand rate for A100-equivalent is $2.40/hr per GPU (list). Current reserved baseline across customers averages ~30% discount; 38% off for a 12-month immediate-sign seems aggressive but within our playbook for strategic accounts.
- If we offer 38% off on a new 12-month sub-commit, we should: require minimum 10% annual spend uplift clause OR include a small ramp guarantee (e.g., commit to 80% of the added capacity within 60 days) to avoid deadhead GPUs.
- SLA: 99.9% regional throughput SLO with a credit formula (X% credit per 1 hr below SLO) is fine; draft metric must reference p95 token latency or sustained tokens/sec.
- Pro-rate approach for short-term augmentation: use calendar-days proration and invoice the remainder term upfront as a one-time charge (preferred for cashflow).

Suggest we present both options but make the step-up commit the "recommended" one with tangible discount and an exit path for them.

I'll run numbers and drop a pricing worksheet.

— Karthik
VP, Sales Operations

Quoting note: if we include a 12-month commit, margin floor requires we maintain at least 22% gross margin; pricing team will mark final numbers accordingly.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Price <samuel.price@edgecloud.ai>
Cc: Maya Rao <maya.rao@edgecloud.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal timeline — midterm capacity add?

Sam —

Attached is a revised proposal and worksheet (Redwood_Proposal_EdgeCloud_v2.xlsx) with both options side-by-side and the following concrete terms:

Option A — Mid-term augmentation (prorated):
- +12 A100-equivalent GPUs added Apr 15 — Dec 31 (10.5 months)
- Rate: on-demand * 0.75 (25% off)
- Invoice: pro-rated one-time charge on Apr invoice
- SLA: standard throughput guidance; no formal credit unless we upgrade to option B

Option B — 12-month step-up commit (recommended):
- +12 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved Apr 15 — Apr 14 2029
- Annualized committed rate: on-demand * 0.62 (38% off) if signed within 14 days from this email; after that window rate moves to on-demand * 0.66 (34% off)
- SLA: 99.9% regional throughput for sustained 1-hour windows. Missed SLOs accrue service credits redeemable against future invoices. Metric defined as sustained tokens/sec per region (p95 latency target included in appendix).
- Ramp clause: must reach 80% utilization of the added pool within 60 days; otherwise we revisit pricing or convert to pro-rate billing.
- Early termination: pro-rata refund/charge depending on usage and reserved counts.

Discount flexibility: we can add a one-time sign-up credit of $15k against the first invoice in lieu of deeper upfront discount, useful if procurement prefers capex smoothing vs immediate discount.

Next actions I suggest: you review Option B with procurement; if they want the commit we can push a clean amendment (attached draft). If they need legal changes, Marcus will own amendment redlines.

— Jonas

Attachments: Redwood_Proposal_EdgeCloud_v2.xlsx; Amendment_Doc_Draft.docx

From: Samuel Price <samuel.price@edgecloud.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Maya Rao <maya.rao@edgecloud.ai>
Cc: contracts@edgecloud.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timeline — midterm capacity add?

Jonas —

Thanks — reviewed with procurement and finance. They prefer Option B (12-month step-up). A few procurement asks:
- Can you confirm the exact on-demand baseline rate you're using in the worksheet (we need it in the amendment)?
- Can the 14-day signature window be extended to 21 days (procurement is slow — but we can expedite internal approval if we have a 3-week window)?
- Can the ramp clause be softened to 60% utilization in 90 days instead of 80% in 60 days?

They are also evaluating your $15k sign-up credit vs an additional 1% off the committed rate. Which is easier to implement?

Please confirm and we'll route the amendment.

— Samuel

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Price <samuel.price@edgecloud.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Mar 2028 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timeline — midterm capacity add?

Sam —

Appreciate the quick feedback. Confirmations below and proposed concessions so we can keep this moving:
- On-demand baseline used in worksheet: $2.40/hr per A100-equivalent GPU. We'll include that explicitly in the amendment.
- Signature window: we can extend to 21 days (one-time extension) but need an internal approval flag; Karthik — please flag this as an exception against the pricing playbook.
- Ramp clause: accepted — revised to 60% utilization within 90 days. We'll update the amendment language.
- Sign-up credit vs 1% off: operationally easier for billing to add the $15k one-time credit (applied to first invoice). If EdgeCloud prefers a permanent 1% additional discount instead, we can do that but it will require an updated margin review. Which does procurement prefer?

Marcus — can you kick off the amendment redline with the explicit baseline rate and the revised ramp/signature windows? I will send a clean DocuSign once legal approves.

If all good from procurement, I'll mark Option B as the committed path and prepare the signature packet.

— Jonas

On Tue, Mar 7, 2028 at 15:10 Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Jonas/Karthik — I'll draft the amendment and target a redline back by EOD tomorrow. Will include the on-demand baseline and revised ramp/signature language.
>
> — Marcus

--- End of thread ---
